prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its biologically active form, which made possible incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange my preferred configuration is unchanged: a single prize part on B022 for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The case is a specific discovery chain, not a body of work: proglucagon processing and the incretin effect, human GLP-1 physiology (Holst), identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide (Mojsov), and peptide biology and translational rationale (Drucker). It has been confirmed in human physiology, independent randomized outcome trials and routine care for glycaemia, body weight and cardiovascular and renal endpoints. Nobody in round 1 raised a maturity objection, and I see none. The six openings agreeing is not my reason. The reasons are the specificity of the discovery and the hard clinical outcomes. I also think a single-part prize is the cleaner choice. A second part would force B022 down to two names, and the dossier gives me no scientific ground for deciding which of the three should go.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weak point and round 1 did not resolve it. Habener is outside the credited names, Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is contested in the public record, and Knudsen's peptide engineering, which produced liraglutide and semaglutide, is excluded by the three-person limit. I have not verified the priority record and none of my colleagues claims to have done so. The honest position is that the supplied evidence supports a physiology-and-active-peptide citation for these three names but cannot settle priority beyond doubt. A critic can also say the prize honours the hormone and not the medicine. The citation is therefore worded narrowly on discovery, so that it does not claim more than the credited names did. If the committee found the Mojsov question disqualifying on documented evidence, I would move to B050 rather than rebuild B022 on guesses.

responses.point: Perlmann says Mojsov's inclusion rests on a disputed priority question he cannot settle from the ballots, and that omitting Knudsen makes a purely physiological citation look incomplete.
responses.response: I share the discomfort on priority, and I agree the ballots cannot settle it. I would still keep Mojsov. The credited record ties her to the synthesis and identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, which is what turned an unresolved precursor-gene finding into a hormone with a defined action. Without her the citation loses that step and rests on Holst and Drucker alone. I have now moved partway to your view on Knudsen. In round 1 I called her exclusion a substantive cost. I now think the right response is a citation that names only what the three laureates did and does not imply that it covers drug development. I would record in our minutes that development credit is not being judged here. I do not think the three-person limit alone justifies changing the discovery being recognised.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius argues the physiological discovery is original and separable from the later drug engineering, and that unanimous opening support shows attractiveness and not that the allocation is right.
responses.response: I agree with both points, and the second is why I put attribution first in my own case against. On separability, I think you are right that this is what makes a discovery-focused citation honest, because the physiology stands on its own findings in humans and the drug work builds on it. Where I would press back is on your suggestion in the uncertainties that CAR-T might share the prize. I can see it as a second part, but it would force B022 to two names, and I do not see how we would choose between Drucker, Holst and Mojsov without making an attribution judgment the dossier cannot support. I would sooner keep B022 whole and hold B003 as the alternative.

responses.point: El Manira names B003 as his fallback if the GLP-1 priority record were judged too unsettled, and calls the medical consequence of the unfolded protein response indirect.
responses.response: The indirectness point is fair and I accept it. The UPR has a clean Mori and Walter attribution and strong mechanistic confirmation, but its disease link runs through diabetes, neurodegeneration and secretory physiology and is less direct than a cell therapy or an incretin drug. That has moved my second alternative. I now list B003 alongside B050 and not B006, which I had in round 1, mainly because the mTOR allocation is unsettled and some colleagues have raised concerns about a candidate that the files do not document. I will not weigh an undocumented concern. I would still note for B003 that the original chimeric-receptor concept is outside the credited names, so I would want June and Sadelain worded fairly to earlier work before treating it as a firm fallback.

responses.point: Sandberg sees Knudsen's drug design as a different kind of work, more naturally recognised separately, and weighs proven patient benefit in keeping CAR-T slightly ahead of the UPR.
responses.response: I accept the logic that drug design is a different achievement from discovery of the physiology and that separate recognition is possible. I would be careful about relying on it, since Nobel practice rarely offers a second chance, as Linnarsson noted. On ranking CAR-T ahead of the UPR, you have persuaded me that proven benefit should count for more, and that is why B003 is now among my alternatives. I still read the early-originator gap as a real weakness for B003 this year, and Perlmann's June and Sadelain version is the only one I would accept. I would not choose between B003 and B050 as a second part unless B022 were unavailable, because the three-person ceiling makes any two-part prize a trade against GLP-1.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1 peptide and Habener's absence from the credited names would change the allocation if the full priority record could be examined. I cannot verify it from the supplied evidence.
Whether leaving out Knudsen is acceptable once the citation is limited to discovery, or whether the committee would prefer a two-part prize despite the cost to B022.
Which of B003 (June and Sadelain, with the early chimeric-receptor work uncredited) or B050 (Mori and Walter, with indirect medical impact) is the better fallback.
Whether the undocumented concerns about a TOR candidate can be assessed at all, which affects whether B006 can be considered.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent for B022, B050 or B003. For disclosure, I have roughly twenty co-authored works with Thomas Perlmann, a fellow committee member (count not audited), on dopamine neurons, Nurr1 and autophagy, unrelated to any shortlisted candidate. I also did a postdoctoral fellowship with Paul Greengard, who is not a shortlisted name. I do not see either as requiring recusal, and shared Karolinska Institutet affiliation is not treated as a conflict.
